title: Platform resilient request primitives: idempotency-first retries, hedged fetches, and deterministic backoff policy
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Goal: Define and implement a single, auditable platform contract for client-side failure recovery that spans services and SDKs. This includes: a standard idempotency key header and TTL semantics, hedged request support for latency SLOs, and a deterministic backoff/backoff-with-jitter family that integrates with circuit-breaker state and server capacity signals. The contract should enable libraries across JS/Python/Go and the runtime to behave consistently so that higher-level product rollouts rely on predictable tail latency and bounded duplicate side effects.
acceptance_criteria: A single HTTP header name is adopted across services (Idempotency-Key) and documented with storage/expiration semantics.
SDKs (JS/Python/Go) expose a consistent idempotency API and enable hedged requests opt-in per-call and per-client.
Backoff algorithm documented: base exponential backoff + decorrelated jitter, plus adaptive floor based on service p95 latency and circuit-breaker open percentage.
Runtime honors Idempotency-Key upsert semantics for write endpoints and returns deterministic status for retries (202/200/409 as defined in spec).
Canary rollout for SDK hedging with telemetry shows <= 1% duplicate side effect rate for calls without idempotency keys and near-zero duplicates when keys provided.
Dashboards for duplicate side effects, hedged request ratio, retry volume, and client-side latency tail are created in Grafana and linked from the Console.
Migration guide and deprecation timeline for legacy retry headers provided to partner teams.
Security review completed and KMS/HSM considerations for idempotency-key storage addressed in private deployments.
Automated tests that simulate region failover and circuit-breaker trips covering hedging, backoff, and idempotent retries included in CI.
implementation_notes: Header: Use 'Idempotency-Key' (RFC-style capitalized) and accept up to 64 ASCII chars; SDKs generate UUIDv4 if not supplied for write operations when configured to ensure safe retries.
Server-side TTL: store key result for at least 24 hours by default; allow per-route override via service config. Expiry must be configurable for on-prem deployments with limited storage.

Idempotency semantics: for POST-like endpoints, server should dedupe by key and return the original response body and status code when duplicate received; if original still processing, return 202 with location header pointing to status endpoint.

Hedged requests: SDKs implement hedging as sending a secondary parallel request after hedging_delay ms if primary not completed; default hedging_delay set per-route using SLO targets (suggest 120ms for chat/generation endpoints), configurable at client and route-level.

Backoff policy: base_backoff_ms = 50, multiplier = 2.0, max_backoff_ms = 5000, jitter = 'decorrelated' (per Exponential Backoff with Full Jitter RFC), and adaptive_floor_ms = max( base_backoff_ms, 0.5 * runtime.p95_latency_ms ). The SDK queries runtime health endpoint for p95 estimate when available.

Integration with Circuit Breaker: when circuit-breaker enters 'open', client switches to longer polling/backoff and disables hedging for non-idempotent calls; for idempotent calls hedging can be preserved depending on 'allow_hedge_when_open' flag on service config.

SDK API design: provide unified call options {idempotencyKey?: string, hedging?: {enabled: boolean, delayMs?: number}, retryConfig?: 'platform-default' | custom}. Expose telemetry hooks for tracing hedged spans.
Telemetry: emit events 'retry.attempt', 'retry.success', 'retry.duplicate_detected', 'hedge.sent', 'hedge.winner', 'idempotency.hit' with tags for route, region, client_version, and circuit_state.
Backwards compatibility: if service does not support Idempotency-Key, SDK falls back to existing retry logic but logs a warning; migration guides required.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 – Design (1 week): finalize header, TTL, and server contract with API owners. Confluence spec: https://confluence.internal/redwood/resilient-primitives

Phase 1 – Runtime & Server adapters (2 weeks): implement idempotency storage sidecar, server middleware to honor keys, and expose health/p95 endpoint. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421

Phase 2 – SDK shims (2 weeks): release v0.10 SDKs with opt-in hedging and platform-default retryConfig. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/412, https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-py/pull/198, https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/77
Phase 3 – Canary (2 weeks): enable idempotency for internal integrations and run hedging at 10% traffic for low-risk routes. Monitor duplicates, tail-latency, and error budget burn.
Phase 4 – Gradual enablement (4 weeks): increment traffic and enable on selected customer tiers; provide opt-out hooks for enterprise Private deploys.
Phase 5 – Enforce (post-migration): deprecate legacy retry headers after 90 days and flip platform-default to 'enabled' for hedging on read-heavy endpoints.
Rollback: feature flags in Console to disable hedging globally per-cluster; SDK exposes runtime-config flags for emergency disable.
risks_and_mitigation: Increased duplicate side effects: mitigate by making hedging opt-in for non-idempotent operations and educating SDK consumers to provide Idempotency-Key for writes.
Storage blowup from idempotency keys: store compact hashes and TTL windows; allow route-level TTL tuning and eviction policies in on-prem configs.
Latency regressions from hedging: limit hedging to routes with SLO-driven thresholds and add rate-limiter on hedged traffic per-client to avoid amplification.
SDK complexity across languages: keep top-level API surface tiny and implement shared behavior in a common spec + test-suite; publish conformance tests.
Security concerns for key leakage: treat idempotency keys as non-sensitive by default but add opt-in encryption-at-rest for Private deployments; document best practices.
test_plan: Unit tests for backoff math and jitter distribution in each SDK.
Integration test that replays network partitions and validates only one side-effect occurs when idempotency key present.
Chaos tests: force region failover and assert hedged request winner selection and latency improvement metrics.
Performance test: measure p50/p95/p99 for generation endpoints with and without hedging at 5%, 10%, 25% hedging rates.
Conformance test-suite for services to verify Idempotency-Key storage/lookup behavior.
notes: This ticket aims to unify disparate retry behaviors observed in telemetry: notably JS SDK was using linear backoff with no jitter and Go SDK used fixed delays. Standardizing reduces system-wide amplification and makes SLO-based tuning practical.
